header.incumbent: Homegrown billing system, built by a former employee
header.tag_why: Owen asked for a customer-specific payback number to get past Diane, we only sent a generic ROI deck, and the planned session never happened before the freeze.

messaging_changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
messaging_changes.change: For product and engineering leads replacing a homegrown billing system: Stop pricing changes from being a tax on the roadmap. Change a price in a few clicks, not a quarter of engineering time.
messaging_changes.why: The buyer rejected the revenue-growth framing outright and described billing as a drain on the roadmap, and their engineers responded to that concrete cost.

messaging_changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
messaging_changes.change: For finance buyers: We build a payback case from your own cost of the current billing system (engineering hours, billing errors, lapsed subscriptions), ready to take to your CFO.
messaging_changes.why: The champion said he could not get the project past the CFO without a customer-specific number, and the team never built one, so the generic study did not carry the deal.

messaging_changes.change: Staged migration timed to your renewal season, so existing landlord cards are not re-collected, plus a reference customer who has done the same migration.
messaging_changes.why: The buyer ruled out touching billing outside renewal season and asked for a migration reference, and our generic timing doc did not answer either request.

trigger.insight: No event started this deal. It was a VP's chronic pain with no deadline attached, so urgency was never set. The only real shift came late, when finance needed payback, which is a different trigger from the one that opened the deal.
trigger.messaging: Pitch against the recurring cost of the homegrown system (every pricing change takes a quarter) rather than a launch deadline, since this buyer never had one.

decider.insight: Diane was the real gate and no one on our side ever spoke to her. Owen's own words say the project could not pass her without a customer-specific number, so our champion was carrying a case he could not finish.
decider.messaging: Give champions a finance-ready, customer-specific business case early so they can take it to the CFO without us in the room.

competitor.insight: The real competitor was the status quo, which costs nothing to keep and wins whenever budgets tighten. The rep's 'as far as I know' means we never confirmed whether Owen looked at other vendors or considered building in-house.
competitor.messaging: Frame the decision as the cost of keeping the homegrown system versus switching, because the status quo is the actual alternative in this market.

message.insight: The demo landed with product and engineering because it removed a concrete drag on the roadmap. Our revenue framing was rejected outright by Owen, which contradicts the rep's claim that nothing got silence.
message.messaging: Replace M7 with copy about removing pricing-change drag, such as changing prices in a few clicks instead of a quarter of engineering, and drop the growth-revenue line for this buyer.

decided.insight: The deal reached procurement with paper sent, but it died on a budget freeze after a Q3 miss, not a choice against us. The month between Owen's payback request and the freeze was the window to build the number, and it went unused, so the value case arrived too late for procurement.
decided.messaging: Make a customer-specific payback case a required step before procurement so a budget review cannot stall the deal on it.

gaps.insight: They asked for their own cost number and a staged migration that avoids re-collecting landlord cards, plus a reference who had done it. We sent a generic study and a timing doc, and the ROI session never happened. The lapsed landlord subscriptions are a revenue leak we never quantified, which is the kind of number finance responds to.
gaps.messaging: Ship a cost-of-current-system worksheet and a staged-migration plan built around renewal season, backed by a reference, before the business case stage.

language.insight: Owen and Diane framed the problem in cost and priority terms, while our copy speaks in growth and revenue terms that the buyer rejected. The rep's 'For Owen, yeah' concedes urgency only at the sponsor level, not the funder level.
language.messaging: Use 'tax on the roadmap' and cost-of-waiting language in billing copy, and address the 'nice to have' objection directly in materials aimed at finance buyers.

gaps.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Owen whether Diane has seen any cost numbers and what her criteria are for approving a project like this.

gaps.question: What did the customer bring up about the competitor?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Owen whether he looked at other billing vendors or considered building in-house.

gaps.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee which claims Owen or his team challenged, and whether any finance stakeholder ever saw the deck.

gaps.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Owen what the homegrown system costs in engineering hours and billing errors per year, and how many landlord subscriptions lapse.

gaps.question: Did Owen get the migration reference he asked for?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee whether a reference was offered and whether Owen took the call.

gaps.question: Did the planned ROI session get scheduled before the Q3 close?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee when the session was proposed and what blocked it from being scheduled.

gaps.question: Is the project coming back next year?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Owen whether the next budget cycle has a date and what Diane would need to see to fund it.

close.rep_takeaway: Get the economic buyer on a call before procurement and build the customer's own cost number with the champion from week one, because a generic ROI deck and a missed session left Owen stuck. Log a budget freeze as a no-decision and ask what would have funded the project, instead of arguing that it was not against us.
